name: Forcepoint
evidence_summary: Forcepoint sources evidence managed Secure SD-WAN, cloud central management, zero-touch deployment, MultiLink resilience and security controls.
cost_model: Quote-based appliances/software/subscriptions; managed SD-WAN positioned but pricing public transparency limited.
key_differentiators: FlexEdge Secure SD-WAN combines secure SD-WAN with strong DLP and data security heritage from the wider Forcepoint portfolio.
MultiLink resilience and zero-touch deployment with cloud central management.
Strong story for buyers prioritising data security and DLP as a procurement criterion.
best_fit_for: Enterprises with strong data protection and DLP requirements (regulated industries, government).
Organisations wanting secure SD-WAN where data security is the primary decision driver.
Buyers consolidating DLP with SD-WAN under one vendor.
watch_outs: Smaller SD-WAN market presence than the leading platforms.
Full SASE platform completeness has partial public evidence; SSE module depth should be confirmed.
Managed delivery is partner-led; co-managed and white-label support require partner validation.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason stated. Sources found and rejected are listed in the evidence register at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: AI Mesh for data security; risk-adaptive protection scores user behaviour in real time.

resilience.note: Cloud SSE with regional redundancy; Secure SD-WAN appliances deploy in HA pairs.

profile.platform_architecture: Forcepoint pairs its long-running Secure SD-WAN (NGFW heritage from Stonesoft) with the Forcepoint ONE SSE platform. Secure SD-WAN appliances cluster natively for high availability and are managed centrally through the Security Management Center, with strength in multi-link, multi-ISP branch designs. Forcepoint ONE delivers SWG, CASB and ZTNA from a cloud platform built on a security-first architecture.
profile.security_sase: Forcepoint's differentiation is data security: market-leading DLP with unified policy from endpoint to cloud, risk-adaptive protection that adjusts enforcement to user behaviour, and AI Mesh data classification. ZTNA, SWG and CASB are delivered through Forcepoint ONE with the DLP engine underneath. For data-centric and government-adjacent buyers, the data security depth is the reason to shortlist.
profile.service_support_channel: Channel-led with government and defence heritage (the Raytheon lineage shows in certifications and clearances), strong in regulated sectors. UK presence is established, with managed offers through security MSPs. Support runs 24x7 with professional services for DLP programmes, which benefit from expert deployment.
profile.commercials_verdict: Per-user SSE licensing and appliance subscriptions, quote based. The Netify verdict: shortlist Forcepoint when data loss prevention is the primary driver, in regulated or government-adjacent estates, or when risk-adaptive enforcement maps to your insider-risk programme. Buyers prioritising WAN routing breadth or the largest PoP fabrics will weight other criteria more heavily.

vendor_faqs.a: One policy engine spans endpoint, network and cloud, with mature fingerprinting, OCR and exact data matching, plus risk-adaptive protection that tightens enforcement as user risk rises. Few rivals match the depth for serious data security programmes.

vendor_faqs.q: Is Forcepoint Secure SD-WAN still developed?
vendor_faqs.a: Yes. The NGFW-based Secure SD-WAN line continues with central management and native clustering, particularly strong for multi-ISP branch resilience in security-conscious estates, and it integrates with Forcepoint ONE for cloud security.

Government and public sector, defence supply chain, financial services and any organisation where data protection obligations lead the architecture. The certification heritage and DLP depth align with those procurement requirements.

shortlist_summary: Forcepoint offer FlexEdge Secure SD-WAN combining secure SD-WAN with DLP and data security capability drawn from the wider Forcepoint portfolio, and for organisations where DLP is a hard procurement requirement rather than an optional extra, that combination is meaningful. Typically shortlisted specifically for data security depth rather than as a general-purpose SD-WAN evaluation.
cost_note: Per-user SSE and appliance subscriptions; mid pricing, with DLP depth the value driver.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US). UK delivery via security partners; government and defence heritage suits UK public sector.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: A managed SD-WAN is a service where a provider handles the deployment, configuration, monitoring and optimisation of your WAN.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Forcepoint's own SD-WAN page defines managed SD-WAN generically as something 'a provider' delivers, and does not claim Forcepoint itself designs, deploys, monitors and reports on the service end to end. The partner programme page frames managed services as certified partner revenue. No Forcepoint-operated fully managed offer was found on the vendor pages reviewed.

f03_co_managed_service.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Checked the Secure SD-WAN product page, the NGFW product page and datasheet, the Cybersecurity Services page, the Implementation Packages page, the Technical Support Offerings datasheet and the Global Partner Program page. No description of a shared responsibility or co-managed operating model was located.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: Forcepoint Administrative Domain License enables multiple customer environments to be managed through a single management server.
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: The SD-WAN Manager datasheet evidences tenant isolation and delegated administration: it also states 'Allows division of the environment into isolated configuration domains' and names MSSPs directly. Graded partial rather than yes because no evidence of branded or white-label portals was found on any page reviewed, and the partner programme page contains no MSP, MSSP, white label or multi-tenant terms.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: Resources and deliverables aligned to your deployment needs and timeline
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: Packaged implementation services and consulting are published, and the Cybersecurity Services page lists 'Implementation Packages for our award-winning products' and 'Data Security Consulting customized to your organization's needs'. Graded partial because the pages reviewed do not describe discovery, pilots, staging, migration runbooks or rollback plans.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: Next Generation Firewall (NGFW) appliances (both N and S-series) now have RMA support included
f07_lifecycle_management.note: Hardware replacement is included in the support contract, with an option to 'upgrade to next business day or same day RMA service'. The SD-WAN Manager datasheet adds 'Upgrades and dynamic update packages for managed devices can be automatically downloaded' and 'Remote Upgrades One-click fail-safe remote upgrade of the managed engines'. Graded partial because upgrades and patching are customer-executed platform features rather than work performed for the customer as part of a service, and no end-of-life planning service was found.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: For LTE without Wi-Fi, Forcepoint offers the 120L model with LTE support and 125L model with LTE/5G support.
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: The 120 Series datasheet also states 'Optional Wi-Fi and LTE/5G connectivity' and lists supported LTE and 5G NR band tables, so integrated cellular is a shipped hardware capability. SIM management and signal monitoring specifics were not located in the pages reviewed.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: Forcepoint operates its own cloud web security service and the SWG page lists 'Public cloud elasticity' and 'Distributed enforcement' as features, but none of the pages reviewed (SWG, CASB, Forcepoint ONE, AI Mesh, Trust Center) publish gateway or point of presence infrastructure detail. Graded partial with low confidence for that reason: a firm yes would need a page describing Forcepoint operated gateway locations.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Checked the SWG, CASB, Forcepoint ONE and AI Mesh product pages, the Secure SD-WAN page and the Trust Center. No reference to customer-hosted, dedicated or sovereign points of presence was located.

f21_private_global_backbone.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Checked the Secure SD-WAN page, the NGFW product page and datasheet, the SWG and CASB pages and the AI Mesh page. No claim of a vendor owned or controlled inter-region backbone was located, and no national network claim was found either.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: 24/7 availability for your most critical issues.
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: The Technical Support Offerings datasheet publishes tiered severity response targets ('Severity 1 1 hour' for Essential, 'Severity 1 45 minutes' for Enhanced, 'Severity 1 30 minutes' for Enterprise) and states 'Severity 1 issues use a follow-the-sun approach; Forcepoint technicians are always available'. Graded partial because these are support response commitments only: no uptime percentage, and no latency, jitter, loss or change handling commitments were found in the pages reviewed.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: Forcepoint authors the NGFW software itself. The datasheet also evidences 'Anti-malware sandboxing', 'Granular application control', 'Always-on SD-WAN connectivity for enterprises' and 'URL Filtering (Separate Subscription)'. URL filtering is a chargeable subscription module but runs on the same platform rather than a separate appliance, so the grade remains yes rather than partial.

f40_managed_service_assurance.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The Technical Support Offerings datasheet describes a reactive, severity-driven technical support model with Customer Success Manager and Customer Success Architect roles, but no 24/7 NOC or SOC monitoring the customer service, no incident ownership through to root cause analysis and no structured service review or change governance were described. Checked also the Cybersecurity Services, Implementation Packages and Global Partner Program pages.

delivery_model.quote: A managed SD-WAN is a service where a provider handles the deployment, configuration, monitoring and optimisation of your WAN.
delivery_model.note: Forcepoint authors the product (NGFW / FlexEdge Secure SD-WAN, SMC, DLP, SWG, CASB). Its own SD-WAN page describes managed SD-WAN in the third person as something 'a provider' does, and the partner programme page positions managed services as partner revenue rather than a Forcepoint-operated service. No Forcepoint-operated managed network service page was found in the pages reviewed.

underlay_ownership.quote: Slash networking costs and improve reliability with real-time mixing and matching of local ISP broadband and private MPLS selection.
underlay_ownership.note: Forcepoint's SD-WAN rides transport the customer already buys (local ISP broadband, private MPLS, and cellular via the LTE and 5G appliance models). No page reviewed shows Forcepoint selling, owning or reselling circuits or core routing.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Provide users with safe and reliable access to the internet, wherever they're located
sse_layer_ownership.note: The security stack is Forcepoint's own engineering across Forcepoint DLP, Secure Web Gateway, CASB and the NGFW software rather than a third party's technology resold under the Forcepoint name. No OEM or partner attribution for the security layer was found on any page reviewed. Confidence is medium because the quote evidences a Forcepoint branded cloud web service rather than explicitly stating in-house authorship.

regulatory_documentation.quote: ISO Statement of Applicability and SOC 2 Type II certifications and assessments
regulatory_documentation.note: Frameworks found and named with downloadable documentation: ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 27017:2015, ISO/IEC 27018:2019, SOC 2 Type 2 (with separate reports listed for Forcepoint ONE, Cloud DSPM and Cloud Web), GDPR, plus a 'Forcepoint EU DORA Compliance document' and 'Covered Entity Compliance with HIPAA and Forcepoint Products'. Not found in the pages reviewed: NHS DSPT, NIS2, FedRAMP, Common Criteria, PCI DSS.

pop_count.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. No point of presence, gateway or data centre count is published on the Secure SD-WAN, SWG, CASB, Forcepoint ONE or AI Mesh pages, nor on the Trust Center. No figure could be quoted, so the value stays unknown.

sla_availability_pct.note: No availability percentage was found. The Technical Support Offerings datasheet publishes severity response times only, and the Trust Center lists a 'Forcepoint Service Status' document under continuous monitoring without stating an uptime figure. A support SLA exists but with no published percentage, so this is unknown.
